newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end stunned by export data gloom.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end stunned by export data gloom.

text.p: Singapore's key Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) lost more than one percent on Thursday close after worse-than-expected export figures stunned economists, shocked dealers and sent investors scurrying for the sidelines.
"I'm so depressed by all this bad news," one dealer said, reacting to non-oil domestic export figures for February which showed a 7.9 percent year-on-year fall.
"This is definitely unmitigated bad news," said P.K. Basu, director of regional economics at UBS Securities.
The STII ended down 25.13 at 2,095.43, a low for the year.
Closing below the psychologically important 2,100 level led to predictions of the fall continuing in the short term.
"If we get into a real bearish mood, we could fall to 2,050 or below," a local dealer said.
The bad news saw losing issues race ahead of gainers by 343 to 74 on mild volume of 170.1 million shares, with blue chips Fraser & Neave and Cycle & Carriage among the hardest hit.
Both lost Singapore $0.20 to end at S$11.70 and S$14.70 respectively while FJ Benjamin slumped S$0.235 to a year low of S$0.905 after reporting disappointing half-year profits.
